entries.test: Riverside's customer emails, subscription prompts, and interface records would show the frequency and prominence of upselling its AI services before publication.
entries.note: The proposition extracts the factual upselling allegation separately from his disgust.
The claim depends on what would have happened under an alternative approach to media coverage.

entries.test: Published ChatGPT coverage would show whether outlets described it as a revolution without substantive explanation, repeated corporate narratives, and dismissed critics.
entries.note: This describes observable patterns in coverage.

entries.test: Dated product documentation and demonstrations would establish whether multiple other companies offered GPT-3-equivalent functionality months before ChatGPT launched.
entries.note: The comparison is explicitly to GPT-3, not to ChatGPT's full interface or product.

entries.test: Public adoption timelines, media coverage, and evidence about acquisition channels would test whether media promotion alone drove ChatGPT's takeoff.
entries.note: “Only” makes this an exclusive causal claim that evidence of independent drivers could contradict.
“I still can’t find” does not establish that no journalist has supplied an explanation. What qualifies as a “cogent” explanation also lacks a shared test.

entries.test: Public audience research, surveys, and studies of media exposure would test whether media narratives predominantly drive demand for AI coverage.
entries.note: “Largely driven” allows independent public demand; the proposition's “not by” excludes it.

entries.test: Documented sustained uses of ChatGPT that deliver practical benefits would test the assertion that it has no real use cases or killer application.
entries.note: He asserts the lack of a killer app, but presents the use-case clause as a rhetorical question. The proposition turns both into categorical assertions.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures or credible financial reporting allocating annual costs and revenue to ChatGPT would establish whether it burns billions of dollars annually.
entries.note: OpenAI-wide losses alone would not establish the amount attributable to ChatGPT.
The recommendation is explicit, but “should note” converts the rhetorical invitation to discuss use cases into a requirement to state their absence as fact.
“Half-broken bullshit” is an insult without a definite product claim. The proposition also removes “appear” from the comparison with consumer reporting.
The extracted claim ranks the importance of stories. He does not endorse Amodei's prediction.

entries.test: Public customer complaints, company responses, and product release histories would show whether companies respond to broken-product complaints by adding generative AI while leaving the defects unresolved.
entries.note: The source caricatures companies proposing AI when consumers look to them. The proposition adds actual implementation and an explicit failure to fix the products.
